watering.title: Watering & Irrigation
watering.summary: Keep hibiscus soil consistently moist but well drained. Do not allow the root zone to remain continuously waterlogged.
guidance: 🌱 Check the top 2–3 cm of soil before watering. Water when the surface begins to feel slightly dry.
💧 Water slowly around the root zone so moisture reaches the deeper soil.
☀️ Increase watering attention during hot, sunny and dry weather.
🌧️ Reduce watering when rainfall has already kept the soil moist.
🪴 Container-grown hibiscus may need more frequent watering because pots dry faster than garden soil.
🌿 Water thoroughly rather than giving very small amounts repeatedly.
🌅 Water preferably during the cooler part of the day so the plant can use the moisture efficiently.
🍂 Mulching around the plant can help reduce moisture loss, but keep mulch away from direct contact with the stem.
🚫 Do not allow the pot to stand continuously in collected water.
irrigation: 💧 Apply water directly to the soil around the root zone instead of repeatedly wetting the foliage.
🪴 Make sure containers have adequate drainage holes.
🌱 For garden plants, slow and deep irrigation is preferable to frequent shallow watering.
💦 Drip or soaker irrigation can provide moisture directly to the root zone.
🌧️ After heavy rainfall, check soil moisture before irrigating again.
🔥 During very hot periods, monitor the soil more frequently rather than following a fixed schedule.
watering.frequency: Usually around 2–4 times per week, but actual frequency depends on temperature, rainfall, soil type, drainage, plant size and container size.
signs_of_underwatering: 🪴 Very dry soil pulling away from the sides of the container
signs_of_overwatering: 💧 Soil remaining wet for long periods
🦠 Increased risk of root and fungal problems
watering.warning: ⚠️ Hibiscus needs regular moisture but not waterlogged soil. Large changes between very dry and very wet conditions can contribute to stress and bud drop.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Hibiscus generally grows and flowers well with full sun or strong bright light.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for around 6 hours or more of direct sunlight when growing conditions allow.
🌸 Good sunlight supports healthy growth and flowering.
🌅 Morning sunlight is beneficial and can provide strong light with less intense afternoon heat.
🔥 During periods of extreme heat, monitor the plant for heat and water stress.
🏡 Keep container hibiscus in a bright location with good air circulation.
🌿 Avoid placing the plant in deep shade for long periods.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Insufficient sunlight may result in weak growth, reduced flowering and excessive stretching.

temperature.title: Temperature & Humidity
temperature.summary: Hibiscus prefers warm growing conditions and regular moisture.
temperature.ideal_range: Approximately 18°C to 32°C for general growing conditions.
guidance: 🌱 Protect tropical hibiscus from prolonged cold conditions.
🔥 Monitor water needs carefully during hot weather.
🌬️ Good airflow helps reduce excessive humidity around the foliage.
💧 Regular moisture is important during active growth.
🌡️ Sudden temperature changes can stress the plant.
❄️ Protect tropical hibiscus from frost and very cold conditions.
temperature.humidity: Moderate to high humidity is generally tolerated by hibiscus, but good airflow should be maintained to reduce prolonged leaf wetness.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ Sudden temperature changes, heat stress and irregular watering may contribute to leaf drop or flower-bud drop.

soil.title: Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile, organic-matter-rich soil that retains reasonable moisture while draining excess water.
recommended_mix: 🌱 Good-quality garden soil or suitable potting mix
🏖️ Coarse material such as sand, perlite or another drainage-improving component when needed
soil_features: 🌬️ Good air movement through the root zone
🚫 Avoid soil that remains saturated for long periods
soil.pH_guidance: A slightly acidic to near-neutral growing medium is generally suitable. Avoid making large pH adjustments without a soil test.
soil.warning: ⚠️ Poor drainage can contribute to root problems, while extremely dry soil can cause water stress.

fertilizer.title: Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🌱 A complete balanced fertilizer such as 13-13-13 or 20-20-20 can be used for general hibiscus growth. 🌸 A phosphorus-containing flowering fertilizer may be used when appropriate during active flowering, following the product label.

fertilizer_options.name: Complete Balanced Fertilizer
guidance: Use a complete fertilizer supplying nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
Products such as 13-13-13 or 20-20-20 are examples cited in extension guidance.
Follow the fertilizer label rather than applying a fixed dose to every plant.

fertilizer_options.name: Slow-Release Complete Fertilizer
fertilizer_options.purpose: Steady nutrient supply, especially for container plants
guidance: Use a suitable slow-release product according to its label.
Do not combine repeated high-rate applications with additional fertilizer unless recommended by the product instructions.

fertilizer_options.name: Compost
guidance: Use mature, well-decomposed compost during soil preparation or as a soil amendment.
Mix appropriately into the growing medium.

fertilizer_options.name: Well-Decomposed Farmyard Manure
guidance: Use only well-decomposed material.
Incorporate it into prepared soil rather than placing fresh manure directly against the plant.

flowering_guidance: 🌸 Hibiscus can benefit from appropriate feeding during active growth and flowering.
🧪 A fertilizer with a higher middle number may be used for flowering only when appropriate and according to the product label.
🚫 More fertilizer does not automatically mean more flowers.
🌿 Excessive fertilization can encourage excessive foliage and may contribute to nutrient or salt problems.
nutrient_guidance: 🧪 If nutrient deficiency is suspected, consider soil or plant testing before adding specific nutrients.
🌿 Iron should not be added routinely unless deficiency or a suitable recommendation indicates a need.
fertilizer.schedule: Feed during active growth according to the selected fertilizer label. Frequency varies by fertilizer type; slow-release and liquid fertilizers have different schedules.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Over-fertilization can damage roots, burn leaves and cause nutrient or salt buildup. Never exceed the product label rate.

pruning.title: Pruning
guidance: ✂️ Remove dead, damaged or clearly diseased branches.
🌿 Light pruning can encourage bushier growth.
🌸 Pruning encourages new growth, which can support flowering in suitable hibiscus types.
🧹 Use clean pruning tools.
🦠 Remove clearly infected plant material and dispose of it appropriately.
🌱 Avoid removing large amounts of healthy growth from a severely stressed plant.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Disinfect pruning tools when moving between diseased and healthy plants.

daily: 💧 Check soil moisture during hot or dry weather.
🌡️ Monitor for heat or water stress.
weekly: 🔍 Inspect leaves and stems for pests and disease symptoms.
🌿 Check for mealybugs, whiteflies, aphids, scale, mites, rust and powdery growth.
🧹 Remove fallen diseased leaves where appropriate.
calendar.watering: Water when the upper soil layer begins to dry rather than following a rigid calendar.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding during active growth according to the selected fertilizer label.
calendar.pruning: Remove dead or damaged growth during routine inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Wear gloves when handling fertilizers or plant-protection products.
🧴 Never exceed the product label rate.
🌬️ Apply sprays only under suitable conditions and avoid strong wind.
🐝 Avoid unnecessary pesticide use when pollinators are actively visiting flowers.
👶 Keep fertilizers and crop-protection products away from children and pets.
🚫 Do not combine fertilizers, fungicides or pesticides unless the product labels specifically permit mixing.
important_warning: 🚨 Do not assume every yellow leaf is caused by a nutrient deficiency; watering, pests, diseases and environmental stress can cause similar symptoms.
🚨 Water stress can contribute to bud drop.
🚨 Do not repeatedly increase fertilizer because the plant is not flowering.
🚨 If the plant declines rapidly, inspect the root zone, watering conditions and pests as well as the leaves.

watering.title: Watering & Irrigation
watering.summary: Maintain reasonably consistent soil moisture while avoiding waterlogging.
guidance: 🌱 Check the upper layer of soil before watering.
💧 Water when the soil begins to dry rather than keeping it continuously saturated.
☀️ Increase monitoring during hot and dry weather.
🌧️ Reduce irrigation when rainfall has already supplied sufficient moisture.
🪴 Container-grown chilli may require more frequent watering than plants in the ground.
🌿 Water deeply enough to moisten the root zone.
🌅 Water during the cooler part of the day when practical.
🍂 Mulching can help reduce evaporation and maintain more consistent soil moisture.
irrigation: 💧 Direct water toward the root zone rather than repeatedly wetting leaves.
🌱 Drip or soaker irrigation can help provide consistent root-zone moisture.
🌧️ Check soil moisture after rainfall before irrigating again.
🔥 During heat waves, monitor soil moisture more frequently.
🚫 Avoid prolonged standing water around the roots.
💦 If using irrigation for a crop, adjust frequency according to soil type, weather and plant growth stage.
watering.frequency: Often around 2–3 times per week, but actual frequency depends on temperature, rainfall, soil type, drainage, plant size and container size.
signs_of_underwatering: 🌶️ Poor fruit development when stress is prolonged
watering.warning: ⚠️ Irregular watering and severe moisture stress can affect flowering, fruit set and fruit development.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Chilli generally performs best with strong direct sunlight.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for approximately 6–8 hours of direct sunlight where conditions are suitable.
🌶️ Good light supports healthy vegetative growth, flowering and fruit production.
🌬️ Provide adequate spacing and airflow around plants.
🏡 Avoid growing chilli in deep shade.
🔥 During extreme heat, monitor for heat and water stress.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Insufficient light can result in weak growth and reduced flowering or fruit production.

temperature.title: Temperature & Humidity
temperature.summary: Chilli is a warm-season crop and performs best under warm growing conditions.
temperature.ideal_range: Approximately 20°C to 32°C for general growing conditions.
guidance: 🌱 Protect plants from prolonged cold conditions.
🔥 Monitor irrigation carefully during very hot weather.
🌸 Extreme heat can interfere with flowering and fruit set.
🌬️ Good airflow helps reduce prolonged humidity around foliage.
🌡️ Avoid sudden environmental changes where practical.
temperature.humidity: Maintain good air circulation, particularly where humidity is high. Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ High heat combined with poor watering can cause severe plant stress and affect flowering and fruit development.

soil.title: Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile, loose and well-draining soil with adequate organic matter.
recommended_mix: 🌱 Good-quality garden soil or vegetable potting mix
🍂 Mature compost or other well-decomposed organic matter
🏖️ Sand, perlite or another suitable drainage-improving material when required
soil.pH_guidance: For pepper/chilli production, approximately pH 6.0–6.8 is a commonly recommended range; soil testing is preferable before major pH correction.
soil.warning: ⚠️ Poor drainage can increase root problems and excessive fertilizer accumulation.

fertilizer.title: Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🌱 Use a complete vegetable fertilizer according to soil-test results and crop stage. 🌶️ Nitrogen is important for growth, while phosphorus and potassium should be supplied according to soil fertility and crop requirements.

fertilizer_options.name: Complete Vegetable Fertilizer
guidance: Use a complete N-P-K fertilizer when needed.
Choose the analysis according to soil-test results and local crop recommendations.
Do not assume the same fertilizer rate is suitable for every soil.

fertilizer_options.name: Nitrogen Fertilizer
guidance: Nitrogen can be supplied before planting and later as a side-dress when appropriate.
Crop-stage nitrogen management is more useful than repeatedly applying large amounts.
Avoid excessive nitrogen because it can promote excessive vegetative growth.

fertilizer_options.name: Phosphorus and Potassium Fertilizer
fertilizer_options.purpose: Root development, flowering and fruit production
guidance: Use phosphorus and potassium according to soil-test results.
Do not add high amounts of phosphorus or potassium when the soil already contains sufficient levels.

fertilizer_options.name: Compost or Well-Decomposed Organic Matter
fertilizer_options.purpose: Soil improvement and organic nutrient contribution
guidance: Use mature compost or well-decomposed organic material during soil preparation.
Do not use fresh manure directly around plants.

stage_based_guidance: 🌱 Early growth: provide balanced nutrition sufficient for healthy vegetative development.
🌸 Flowering: maintain adequate nutrition without excessive nitrogen.
🌶️ Fruit development: maintain appropriate potassium and overall nutrition according to soil and crop requirements.
🧪 Soil testing is preferred when deciding phosphorus and potassium applications.
fertilizer.schedule: Apply fertilizer according to soil-test recommendations, crop stage and the selected product label. Split applications may be appropriate for nitrogen during the crop cycle.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Excess fertilizer can burn roots, increase salt concentration and create nutrient imbalance. Do not use a high rate simply to increase plant growth.

pruning.title: Pruning
guidance: ✂️ Remove clearly dead or severely diseased leaves.
🌿 Avoid excessive pruning of a healthy fruiting plant.
🧹 Keep pruning tools clean.
🦠 Remove heavily diseased material and dispose of it appropriately.
🌱 Maintain sufficient healthy foliage for photosynthesis and fruit development.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Avoid removing large amounts of healthy foliage because the plant needs leaves to support growth and fruit production.

daily: 💧 Check soil moisture during hot weather.
🌡️ Monitor plants for heat or water stress.
weekly: 🔍 Inspect leaves and stems for pests and disease symptoms.
🐛 Check the underside of leaves for mites, thrips and other small pests.
🍂 Look for leaf spots, curling, discoloration and nutrient-deficiency symptoms.
calendar.watering: Check soil moisture frequently and adjust irrigation according to weather and plant growth.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding according to crop stage, soil-test results and product instructions.
calendar.pruning: Remove dead or severely affected material during routine inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Wear appropriate protective equipment when applying fertilizers or crop-protection products.
🌬️ Do not spray during strong wind.
🧴 Follow the exact product label and required waiting period before harvest.
🥬 Follow appropriate produce-washing practices after harvest.
🚫 Do not randomly mix pesticides, fungicides or fertilizers.
🐝 Avoid unnecessary pesticide use when pollinators are active.
important_warning: 🚨 Leaf curling can have several causes, including pests, viruses, heat stress and nutrient problems.
🚨 Yellow leaves do not automatically mean that fertilizer is required.
🚨 Check the underside of leaves for mites, thrips and other small pests.
🚨 Do not apply large amounts of fertilizer without considering soil condition and plant symptoms.
🚨 If symptoms spread rapidly, inspect nearby plants and environmental conditions.

watering.title: Watering & Irrigation
watering.summary: Tomatoes perform best with consistent root-zone moisture while avoiding waterlogged soil.
guidance: 🌱 Check soil moisture before watering.
💧 Water deeply enough to moisten the root zone rather than giving frequent shallow amounts.
🌿 Water near the base of the plant rather than repeatedly wetting leaves.
☀️ Increase monitoring during hot and dry weather.
🌧️ Reduce irrigation after sufficient rainfall.
🪴 Use containers with drainage holes.
🌅 Water during the cooler part of the day when practical.
🍂 Mulching can help conserve soil moisture and reduce rapid moisture fluctuations.
🚫 Avoid allowing the soil to remain continuously saturated.
irrigation: 💧 Drip irrigation or soaker irrigation is useful for delivering water directly to the root zone.
🌿 Avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation because wet foliage can encourage some foliar diseases.
🌧️ Check actual soil moisture after rainfall before irrigating.
🔥 During hot periods, monitor plants and soil more frequently.
🌱 Maintain relatively consistent moisture during flowering and fruit development.
💦 Adjust irrigation according to soil type, weather, plant size and container size.
watering.frequency: Often every 1–3 days in hot conditions, but actual frequency depends on weather, soil, plant size, container size and drainage.
signs_of_underwatering: 🍅 Poor fruit development when stress is prolonged
watering.warning: ⚠️ Large fluctuations in soil moisture can stress tomato plants and contribute to some fruit-quality problems.

sunlight.title: Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Tomatoes generally need strong sunlight for vigorous growth and fruit production.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for around 6–8 hours of direct sunlight when possible.
🍅 Strong light supports flowering and fruit development.
🌬️ Provide good airflow between plants.
🏡 Avoid overcrowding container-grown tomatoes.
🔥 Monitor watering during periods of intense heat.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Poor sunlight can result in weak growth and reduced flowering and fruit production.

temperature.title: Temperature & Humidity
temperature.summary: Tomatoes prefer warm growing conditions but can experience stress under extreme temperatures.
temperature.ideal_range: Approximately 18°C to 30°C for general growing conditions.
guidance: 🌱 Protect plants from prolonged cold conditions.
🔥 Monitor water needs carefully during hot weather.
🌸 Very high temperatures can interfere with flowering and fruit set.
🌬️ Maintain good airflow around foliage.
💧 Avoid unnecessarily prolonged leaf wetness.
temperature.humidity: Good air circulation is particularly important when humidity is high because prolonged leaf wetness can increase foliar disease pressure.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ Extreme heat can cause stress and wilting even when the plant does not have a disease.

soil.title: Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile, well-draining soil with adequate organic matter.
recommended_mix: 🌱 Quality garden soil or suitable vegetable potting mix
🏖️ Perlite, coarse material or another drainage-improving component when required
soil.pH_guidance: A soil pH around 6.0–6.8 is commonly recommended for tomato production. Use soil testing before making significant pH adjustments.
soil.warning: ⚠️ Avoid heavily compacted, poorly drained soil and avoid leaving infected plant debris around the growing area.

fertilizer.title: Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🍅 Use a complete tomato/vegetable fertilizer according to soil-test results. A fertilizer with relatively lower nitrogen and adequate phosphorus and potassium can be appropriate for tomatoes. 🌱 Apply additional nitrogen only when crop and soil conditions indicate a need.

fertilizer_options.name: Complete Tomato/Vegetable Fertilizer
guidance: Use a complete fertilizer when soil testing indicates a need.
Tomatoes generally benefit from balanced nutrition with attention to nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
A product such as 10-20-10 is one example used in extension recommendations when soil-test information is unavailable.

fertilizer_options.name: Nitrogen Fertilizer
fertilizer_options.purpose: Vegetative growth and continued crop development
guidance: Apply nitrogen according to soil fertility and crop demand.
Split applications can be used when appropriate during the growing season.
Avoid excessive nitrogen because it can promote excessive vine growth and delay maturity.

fertilizer_options.name: Phosphorus and Potassium Fertilizer
fertilizer_options.purpose: Root development, flowering and fruit development
guidance: Use phosphorus and potassium according to soil-test results.
Potassium is particularly important to maintain adequate nutrition during fruit production.
Do not apply large quantities when soil tests already show sufficient levels.

fertilizer_options.name: Compost or Well-Decomposed Organic Matter
fertilizer_options.purpose: Soil improvement and organic nutrient contribution
guidance: Incorporate mature compost or well-decomposed organic matter into the soil before planting.
Use only well-decomposed manure or organic materials.

stage_based_guidance: 🌱 Before planting: incorporate required nutrients based on soil testing and crop recommendations.
🌿 Early growth: provide enough nutrition for healthy plant establishment without excessive nitrogen.
🌸 Flowering: maintain balanced nutrition and adequate potassium.
🍅 Fruit development: maintain adequate potassium and nitrogen according to crop demand and soil condition.
🧪 Use soil or plant testing when nutrient deficiency or excess is suspected.
fertilizer.schedule: Review feeding according to crop stage, soil-test results and the fertilizer product label. Additional applications should be based on crop demand rather than a fixed high-dose schedule.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Excess nitrogen can produce excessive vegetative growth and may increase some fruit and disease-management problems. Over-fertilization can also damage roots and increase salt buildup.

pruning.title: Pruning and Plant Support
guidance: ✂️ Remove dead or severely diseased leaves where appropriate.
🌿 Keep lower foliage from resting directly on wet soil when possible.
🪢 Support plants using suitable stakes, cages or trellising.
🧹 Keep tools clean when working with multiple plants.
🌱 Avoid removing large amounts of healthy foliage at one time.
🦠 Remove severely infected plant material and dispose of it appropriately.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Excessive removal of healthy foliage can reduce the plant's ability to photosynthesize and support fruit development.

daily: 💧 Check soil moisture, especially during hot weather.
🌡️ Monitor plants for heat or water stress.
weekly: 🍂 Look for early blight, late blight, leaf mold, leaf spots and unusual discoloration.
🐛 Check for whiteflies, aphids and other pests.
calendar.watering: Check soil moisture daily during hot weather and adjust irrigation according to actual conditions.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding according to crop stage, soil condition and fertilizer label instructions.
calendar.pruning: Check and remove dead or severely affected leaves during weekly inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Use protective equipment when handling fertilizers or plant-protection products.
🍅 Follow the required pre-harvest interval for agricultural chemicals.
🐝 Avoid unnecessary chemical treatment when pollinators are active.
🚫 Do not randomly mix fertilizers, fungicides or pesticides.
important_warning: 🚨 Tomato leaf spots can have multiple causes; do not assume every spot is the same disease.
🚨 Early blight and late blight require careful differentiation because management can differ.
🚨 Avoid unnecessary wetting of tomato leaves when foliar disease pressure is high.
🚨 Do not automatically apply fertilizer when leaves turn yellow; check watering, pests, disease and nutrient conditions.
🚨 If symptoms spread rapidly, inspect nearby plants and environmental conditions.
